Central London Office Market Watch Q1 2026 01 May 2026 Article
Leasing across Central London reached 2.2m sq ft across 152 transactions at the end of Q1.
Supply across Central London remained stable over the quarter at 19.1m sq ft
This equates to a vacancy rate of 7.4%
The City vacancy rate remained at the same level at 7.0%
West End market saw a slight contraction to supply, bringing the vacancy rate down 10 bps on the previous quarter to 7.8%
Development completions reached 1.4m sq ft, with nine schemes reaching practical completion by the end of Q1.
average prime rent for the City rose to £130.80 per sq ft.
average prime rent across the West End held steady at £165.00 per sq ft
The largest pre-let (and transaction) to complete was global law firm Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer’s acquisition of British Land and GIC’s 1 Appold Street, EC2 (268,000 sq ft), at £104 per sq ft, for a term of 21 years.
Leasing activity continued to be driven by demand for Grade A office space, which accounted for 92% of Q1 take‑up. This demand was predominantly focused on BREEAM-rated Excellent and Outstanding buildings, which together represented 53% of Q1 take‑up.
There has been a notable shift towards refurbishments, with comprehensive refurbishments accounting for 70% of the number of schemes set for delivery over the next four years (78% by sq ft), up 5% on the proportion at the end of Q1 2025.
